decision: Three steps: what we build, what we buy, what we give up
why: Six cards at once is a table; three focused passes turn it into an argument a founder can follow.
value: The trade-offs land one at a time.

decision: What we give up is always amber, on every card, and amber means nothing else
why: The skill is choosing which cost to accept, so the cost gets its own color.
value: Costs are visible at a glance, never buried.

decision: Cards render from data/build-vs-buy/metrics.json, which tests check for a why, a give-up, a swap plan and cost at 10×
why: The cards, the 80/20 map and the decision log must never disagree.
value: One source of truth; a row without a cost fails the build.

decision: Every bought part has a swap plan and a cost-at-10× note in the engineering layer
why: Buying is only safe when leaving is possible and the bill at 10× is known before it arrives.
value: Vendor choices stay reversible and budgeted.

decision: No row says free without a limit next to it
why: Free tiers end; a plan built on an unbounded free promise is a plan to be surprised.
value: Every cost claim has a bound.
